blocks.en: IP Header
blocks.en_html: IP Header
blocks.zh_html: IP 首部(IP header)

blocks.en: IP Header Design Goals
blocks.en_html: IP Header Design Goals
blocks.zh_html: IP 首部设计目标(IP header design goals)

blocks.en: Recall that a protocol like IP consists of syntax and semantics. The syntax determines what fields are in the IP header, and the semantics determine how those fields are processed.
blocks.en_html: Recall that a protocol like IP consists of syntax and semantics. The syntax determines what fields are in the IP header, and the semantics determine how those fields are processed.
blocks.zh_html: 回想一下，像 IP 这样的协议(protocol)由语法(syntax)和语义(semantics)组成。语法决定了 IP 首部(IP header)中有哪些字段(fields)，而语义决定了这些字段如何处理。

blocks.en: Also, recall that the IP packet consists of a header and payload. The header contains relevant metadata that the IP protocol can process. The payload contains any data that will be passed up to higher-layer protocols, and is not parsed by the IP protocol.
blocks.en_html: Also, recall that the IP packet consists of a header and payload. The header contains relevant metadata that the IP protocol can process. The payload contains any data that will be passed up to higher-layer protocols, and is not parsed by the IP protocol.
blocks.zh_html: 另外，回想一下 IP 分组(IP packet)由首部(header)和载荷(payload)组成。首部包含 IP 协议(IP protocol)可以处理的相关元数据(metadata)。载荷包含将向上传递给更高层协议(higher-layer protocols)的数据，而 IP 协议不会解析(parse)载荷。

blocks.en: Finally, recall that headers are added as we move down the stack, and stripped away as we pass packets up the stack. IP headers are processed at both end hosts, and at every intermediate router.
blocks.en_html: Finally, recall that headers are added as we move down the stack, and stripped away as we pass packets up the stack. IP headers are processed at both end hosts, and at every intermediate router.
blocks.zh_html: 最后，回想一下，首部(headers)在我们沿协议栈向下移动时被添加，在我们将分组向上传递时被剥离。IP 首部(IP headers)在端主机(end hosts)和每一台中间路由器(intermediate router)上都会被处理。

blocks.en: The IP header should be as small as possible. Every packet sent across the Internet need the IP header attached, so increasing the IP header size, even by one byte, would significantly increase the total amount of bandwidth across the Internet.
blocks.en_html: The IP header should be as small as possible. Every packet sent across the Internet need the IP header attached, so increasing the IP header size, even by one byte, would significantly increase the total amount of bandwidth across the Internet.
blocks.zh_html: IP 首部(IP header)应该尽可能小。在互联网(Internet)上传输的每个分组(packet)都需要附加 IP 首部，因此增加 IP 首部大小，即使只增加 1 字节(byte)，也会显著增加整个互联网的总带宽(bandwidth)消耗。

blocks.en: The IP header should be as simple as possible. Every router and end host has to process IP packets as they’re sent and received, so a header that’s complicated to process would slow the entire Internet down. Ideally, we’d like the header to be processed purely in hardware, so we can’t assume we have access to general-purpose CPU operations when processing this header.
blocks.en_html: The IP header should be as simple as possible. Every router and end host has to process IP packets as they're sent and received, so a header that's complicated to process would slow the entire Internet down. Ideally, we'd like the header to be processed purely in hardware, so we can't assume we have access to general-purpose CPU operations when processing this header.
blocks.zh_html: IP 首部(IP header)应该尽可能简单。每台路由器(router)和端主机(end host)在发送和接收 IP 分组(IP packets)时都需要处理首部，因此一个处理复杂的首部会拖慢整个互联网(Internet)。理想情况下，我们希望首部能纯粹在硬件中处理，因此不能假设在处理这个首部时可以依赖通用 CPU 操作。

blocks.en: IP Header Fields
blocks.en_html: IP Header Fields
blocks.zh_html: IP 首部字段(IP header fields)

blocks.en: An IP protocol needs to do four things:
blocks.en_html: An IP protocol needs to do four things:
blocks.zh_html: 一个 IP 协议(IP protocol)需要做四件事：

blocks.en: Everybody (end hosts, routers) need to be able to parse the packet and understand what the bits mean. To support this, the header will include the IP version (4-bit value), the header length (4-bit value, measured in 4-byte words, required because the IP header length is not fixed), and the packet length (16-bit value, measured in bytes).
blocks.en_html: Everybody (end hosts, routers) need to be able to parse the packet and understand what the bits mean. To support this, the header will include the IP version (4-bit value), the header length (4-bit value, measured in 4-byte words, required because the IP header length is not fixed), and the packet length (16-bit value, measured in bytes).
blocks.zh_html: 所有设备（端主机(end hosts)、路由器(routers)）都需要能够解析(parse)分组(packet)并理解这些比特的含义。为了支持这一点，首部(header)将包含IP 版本(IP version)（4 位值）、首部长度(header length)（4 位值，以 4 字节字为单位，因为 IP 首部长度不固定）和分组长度(packet length)（16 位值，以字节为单位）。

blocks.en: Routers (not end hosts) need to forward the packet to the next router. To support this, the header will include the destination IP address (32-bit value).
blocks.en_html: Routers (not end hosts) need to forward the packet to the next router. To support this, the header will include the destination IP address (32-bit value).
blocks.zh_html: 路由器(routers)（而非端主机）需要将分组(packet)转发(forward)到下一台路由器。为了支持这一点，首部(header)将包含目的 IP 地址(destination IP address)（32 位值）。

blocks.en: End hosts (not routers) need to pass the packet up to higher layers. To support this, the header will include a protocol number (8-bit value), which tells us which Layer 4 protocol (TCP or UDP) should be used to process the payload. For example, a protocol number of 6 says to use the TCP protocol to read the remaining payload (reading the first bits of the payload as the TCP header, and so on). A protocol number of 17 corresponds to the UDP protocol.
blocks.en_html: End hosts (not routers) need to pass the packet up to higher layers. To support this, the header will include a protocol number (8-bit value), which tells us which Layer 4 protocol (TCP or UDP) should be used to process the payload. For example, a protocol number of 6 says to use the TCP protocol to read the remaining payload (reading the first bits of the payload as the TCP header, and so on). A protocol number of 17 corresponds to the UDP protocol.
blocks.zh_html: 端主机(end hosts)（而非路由器）需要将分组(packet)向上传递(pass up)到更高层。为了支持这一点，首部(header)将包含一个协议号(protocol number)（8 位值），它告诉我们应使用哪个第 4 层协议(Layer 4 protocol)，即 TCP 或 UDP，来处理载荷(payload)。例如，协议号 6 表示使用 TCP 协议来读取剩余的载荷（将载荷的前几个比特读取为 TCP 首部，依此类推）。协议号 17 对应 UDP 协议。

blocks.en: End hosts and routers need to be able to send replies back to the source. To support this, the header will include the source IP address (32-bit value).
blocks.en_html: End hosts and routers need to be able to send replies back to the source. To support this, the header will include the source IP address (32-bit value).
blocks.zh_html: 端主机(end hosts)和路由器(routers)需要能够向发送方回复(send replies)。为了支持这一点，首部(header)将包含源 IP 地址(source IP address)（32 位值）。

blocks.en: IP Error Handling
blocks.en_html: IP Error Handling
blocks.zh_html: IP 错误处理(IP error handling)

blocks.en: End hosts and routers also need to be able to specify problems or special cases in case a packet needs additional handling.
blocks.en_html: End hosts and routers also need to be able to specify problems or special cases in case a packet needs additional handling.
blocks.zh_html: 端主机(end hosts)和路由器(routers)还需要能够指明问题或特殊情况(specify problems or special cases)，以便分组(packet)需要额外处理时使用。

blocks.en: IP packets can be stuck in loops (e.g. if the routing protocol hasn’t converged yet). One possible option is to let the packet loop indefinitely until routes converge, but packet forwarding happens on nanosecond scale, and routing convergence happens on the millisecond or second scale. Letting the packet loop until routes converge can take a long time and waste a lot of bandwidth. To prevent indefinite looping, the IP header has a time to live (TTL) (8-bit value), which is decremented at each hop. If the TTL reaches 0, the packet is discarded, and an error message is sent back to the source. (The error message is required by the IP specification, though is not always sent in practice.)
blocks.en_html: IP packets can be stuck in loops (e.g. if the routing protocol hasn't converged yet). One possible option is to let the packet loop indefinitely until routes converge, but packet forwarding happens on nanosecond scale, and routing convergence happens on the millisecond or second scale. Letting the packet loop until routes converge can take a long time and waste a lot of bandwidth. To prevent indefinite looping, the IP header has a time to live (TTL) (8-bit value), which is decremented at each hop. If the TTL reaches 0, the packet is discarded, and an error message is sent back to the source. (The error message is required by the IP specification, though is not always sent in practice.)
blocks.zh_html: IP 分组(IP packets)可能陷入环路(loops)，例如路由协议(routing protocol)尚未收敛(converged)时。一种可能的方案是让分组无限循环，直到路由收敛，但分组转发(packet forwarding)在纳秒(nanosecond)级别发生，而路由收敛(routing convergence)在毫秒(millisecond)或秒(second)级别发生。让分组持续循环直到路由收敛可能需要很长时间，并浪费大量带宽(bandwidth)。为了防止无限循环，IP 首部(IP header)中有一个生存时间(TTL)（8 位值），每经过一跳(hop)就减 1。如果 TTL 减到 0，分组被丢弃，并向发送方返回一条错误消息。（IP 规范要求发送错误消息，尽管在实践中并不总是发送。）

blocks.en: IP packets can be corrupted (e.g. bits on the wire can be corrupted from electrical processes). To detect corruption, the IP header contains a checksum (16-bit value), and discards packets if the checksum is incorrect.
blocks.en_html: IP packets can be corrupted (e.g. bits on the wire can be corrupted from electrical processes). To detect corruption, the IP header contains a checksum (16-bit value), and discards packets if the checksum is incorrect.
blocks.zh_html: IP 分组(IP packets)可能被损坏(corrupted)，例如线路上的比特可能因电气过程而损坏。为了检测损坏，IP 首部(IP header)包含一个校验和(checksum)（16 位值），如果校验和不正确，则丢弃分组。

blocks.en: Note that the IP checksum is only computed over the IP header. The checksum can only detect errors in the IP header, not errors in the IP payload. This reflects the end-to-end principle, where we enforce that the payload is checked by the end host, not the intermediate routers.
blocks.en_html: Note that the IP checksum is only computed over the IP header. The checksum can only detect errors in the IP header, not errors in the IP payload. This reflects the end-to-end principle, where we enforce that the payload is checked by the end host, not the intermediate routers.
blocks.zh_html: 注意，IP 校验和(checksum)仅针对 IP 首部(IP header)计算。校验和只能检测 IP 首部中的错误，不能检测 IP 载荷(payload)中的错误。这体现了端到端原则(end-to-end principle)：我们要求载荷由端主机(end host)检查，而非中间路由器(intermediate routers)。

blocks.en: The IP checksum is updated at every router, because the TTL changes, and the checksum has to be re-computed. One possible alternative design is to exclude the TTL in the checksum, to save routers the extra work.
blocks.en_html: The IP checksum is updated at every router, because the TTL changes, and the checksum has to be re-computed. One possible alternative design is to exclude the TTL in the checksum, to save routers the extra work.
blocks.zh_html: IP 校验和(checksum)会在每台路由器(router)上被更新，因为 TTL 会变化，校验和必须重新计算。一种可能的替代设计是，将 TTL 排除在校验和之外，以节省路由器的额外工作。

blocks.en: IP packets could be too large for a specific link. Each link has a maximum transmission unit (MTU), indicating the largest packet size (in bytes) that link can carry as one unit. For example, the link might have limited memory for remembering a packet while it sends the bits along the wire.
blocks.en_html: IP packets could be too large for a specific link. Each link has a maximum transmission unit (MTU), indicating the largest packet size (in bytes) that link can carry as one unit. For example, the link might have limited memory for remembering a packet while it sends the bits along the wire.
blocks.zh_html: IP 分组(IP packets)可能对特定链路(link)来说太大。每条链路有一个最大传输单元(MTU)，表示该链路作为一个单元能承载的最大分组大小（以字节为单位）。例如，链路在沿线路发送比特期间，用于暂存分组的存储器(memory)可能有限。

blocks.en: The end host doesn’t know which links will be carrying the packet, so the end host might sent a packet that’s too large for one of the links. To solve this, a router can perform fragmentation, splitting the packet into multiple fragments, which the router on the other end of the link must reassemble to recover the original packet. The identification (16-bit), flags (3-bit), and offset (13-bit) fields in the header are used to implement fragmentation.
blocks.en_html: The end host doesn't know which links will be carrying the packet, so the end host might sent a packet that's too large for one of the links. To solve this, a router can perform fragmentation, splitting the packet into multiple fragments, which the router on the other end of the link must reassemble to recover the original packet. The identification (16-bit), flags (3-bit), and offset (13-bit) fields in the header are used to implement fragmentation.
blocks.zh_html: 端主机(end host)不知道哪些链路会承载分组，因此可能会发送一个对某条链路来说过大的分组。为了解决这个问题，路由器(router)可以执行分片(fragmentation)，将分组拆分成多个片(fragments)，然后由链路另一端的路由器重组(reassemble)以恢复原始分组。首部(header)中的标识(identification)（16 位）、标志(flags)（3 位）和片偏移(offset)（13 位）字段用于实现分片。

blocks.en: Fragmentation is achievable in hardware (e.g. a router can quickly fragment packets without punting the packet for special handling), but it introduces extra overhead. The modern Internet avoids fragmentation whenever possible. For example, we try to standardize the MTU as much as possible (a modern standard is 1500 bytes).
blocks.en_html: Fragmentation is achievable in hardware (e.g. a router can quickly fragment packets without punting the packet for special handling), but it introduces extra overhead. The modern Internet avoids fragmentation whenever possible. For example, we try to standardize the MTU as much as possible (a modern standard is 1500 bytes).
blocks.zh_html: 分片(fragmentation)可以在硬件中实现，例如路由器可以快速分片而无须将分组移交(punting)给特殊处理，但这会引入额外的开销。现代互联网(Internet)尽可能避免分片。例如，我们尽量标准化 MTU（现代标准是 1500 字节）。

blocks.en: The early designers of IP did not fully embrace best-effort design, and thought it might be useful to allow applications to send packets of different types based on the application’s needs. To implement this, the IP header has Type of Service (ToS) bits (8-bit value), which can be used to request different forms of packet delivery. For example, some packets can be marked as delay-sensitive or high-priority. Over the years, these bits have been redefined to represent different protocols, and ToS no longer exists in its original form. Instead, these bits now represent some notion of priority. Examples of protocols using these bits are Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP), which defines certain classes of traffic, and Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN), which will help with traffic congestion (discussed later).
blocks.en_html: The early designers of IP did not fully embrace best-effort design, and thought it might be useful to allow applications to send packets of different types based on the application's needs. To implement this, the IP header has Type of Service (ToS) bits (8-bit value), which can be used to request different forms of packet delivery. For example, some packets can be marked as delay-sensitive or high-priority. Over the years, these bits have been redefined to represent different protocols, and ToS no longer exists in its original form. Instead, these bits now represent some notion of priority. Examples of protocols using these bits are Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP), which defines certain classes of traffic, and Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN), which will help with traffic congestion (discussed later).
blocks.zh_html: IP 的早期设计者并未完全采纳尽力而为(best-effort)设计，他们认为允许应用(application)根据自身需求发送不同类型的分组(packets)可能是有用的。为了实现这一点，IP 首部(IP header)中有服务类型(ToS)位（8 位值），可用于请求不同形式的分组投递(packet delivery)。例如，某些分组可以标记为延迟敏感(delay-sensitive)或高优先级(high-priority)。多年以来，这些位已被重新定义以表示不同的协议，ToS 不再以其原始形式存在。相反，这些位现在表示某种优先级概念。使用这些位的协议示例包括：区分服务码点(DSCP)，它定义了某些流量类别(traffic classes)；以及显式拥塞通知(ECN)，它将有助于处理流量拥塞(congestion)（将在后面讨论）。

blocks.en: In the original IP design, additional option bits can be added to the IP header to request more advanced processing on the packet. For example, the sender can request routers to record the route that the packet is taking (e.g. for diagnostics). The sender could include a source route in the packet header and force the packet to travel a certain route. The packet header could also include a timestamp. In modern implementations, these options are almost always disabled, because they lead to unnecessarily complicated implementations that increase the packet processing overhead. For example, these options force the IP header to be variable-length, which is harder to process than a fixed-length header.
blocks.en_html: In the original IP design, additional option bits can be added to the IP header to request more advanced processing on the packet. For example, the sender can request routers to record the route that the packet is taking (e.g. for diagnostics). The sender could include a source route in the packet header and force the packet to travel a certain route. The packet header could also include a timestamp. In modern implementations, these options are almost always disabled, because they lead to unnecessarily complicated implementations that increase the packet processing overhead. For example, these options force the IP header to be variable-length, which is harder to process than a fixed-length header.
blocks.zh_html: 在最初的 IP 设计中，可以在 IP 首部(IP header)中添加额外的选项位(option bits)，以请求对分组(packet)进行更高级的处理。例如，发送方可以请求路由器(routers)记录分组经过的路由(route)，例如用于诊断(diagnostics)。发送方可以在分组首部中包含源路由(source route)，强制分组走特定的路径。分组首部还可以包含时间戳(timestamp)。在现代实现中，这些选项几乎总是被禁用，因为它们会导致不必要的复杂实现，增加分组处理开销。例如，这些选项迫使 IP 首部变为可变长度(variable-length)，比固定长度首部更难处理。

blocks.en: IPv6 Header Changes
blocks.en_html: IPv6 Header Changes
blocks.zh_html: IPv6 首部变化(IPv6 header changes)

blocks.en: IPv6 was motivated by the concern that we would eventually run out of 32-bit IPv4 addresses. IPv6 expanded addresses so that addresses are 128 bits long. The number of possible IPv6 addresses is astronomically large (think: number of atoms in the universe), so we will almost certainly never run out of IPv6 addresses.
blocks.en_html: IPv6 was motivated by the concern that we would eventually run out of 32-bit IPv4 addresses. IPv6 expanded addresses so that addresses are 128 bits long. The number of possible IPv6 addresses is astronomically large (think: number of atoms in the universe), so we will almost certainly never run out of IPv6 addresses.
blocks.zh_html: IPv6 的动机是担心我们最终会用完 32 位的 IPv4 地址。IPv6 扩展了地址(expanded addresses)，使地址长度为 128 位(bits)。可能的 IPv6 地址数量大得惊人（想想宇宙中的原子数量），因此我们几乎可以肯定永远不会用尽 IPv6 地址。

blocks.en: The designers of IPv6 took the opportunity to clean up and modernize the IP header, removing and updating fields that are outdated. Originally, IPv6 was intended to be a more ambitious protocol with many new addressing features, but most of these features were never realized. In practice, besides this “spring cleaning” removal of outdated features, there weren’t many significant changes to the protocol from IPv4, so the result is a more elegant IP protocol, without many ambitious changes.
blocks.en_html: The designers of IPv6 took the opportunity to clean up and modernize the IP header, removing and updating fields that are outdated. Originally, IPv6 was intended to be a more ambitious protocol with many new addressing features, but most of these features were never realized. In practice, besides this "spring cleaning" removal of outdated features, there weren't many significant changes to the protocol from IPv4, so the result is a more elegant IP protocol, without many ambitious changes.
blocks.zh_html: IPv6 的设计者借此机会清理和现代化了 IP 首部(IP header)，移除和更新了过时的字段(fields)。最初，IPv6 被设计成一个更雄心勃勃的协议(protocol)，具有许多新的寻址特性(addressing features)，但这些特性大多从未实现。在实践中，除了这种对过时特性的"春季大扫除"之外，该协议相较于 IPv4 并没有太多显著变化，因此结果是得到一个更优雅的 IP 协议，而没有什么雄心勃勃的改变。

blocks.en: Note: In case you’re curious, IPv5 was published in 1990 (before IPv6 in 1998). It was an experimental protocol that was never widely implemented.
blocks.en_html: Note: In case you're curious, IPv5 was published in 1990 (before IPv6 in 1998). It was an experimental protocol that was never widely implemented.
blocks.zh_html: 注意：如果你感到好奇，IPv5 发表于 1990 年（早于 1998 年的 IPv6）。它是一个实验性协议(experimental protocol)，从未被广泛实现。

blocks.en: IPv6 eliminates checksums in the IP packet header. The argument in favor of including a checksum is: if a packet is corrupted and is not detected, the corrupt packet continues being sent, wasting bandwidth. Including the checksum ensures that the packet is dropped and bandwidth is not wasted on a corrupt packet. In modern times, bandwidth is less of a bottleneck, so the checksum is no longer necessary, and it’s not a huge performance impact if some corrupt packets are sent all the way through the network.
blocks.en_html: IPv6 eliminates checksums in the IP packet header. The argument in favor of including a checksum is: if a packet is corrupted and is not detected, the corrupt packet continues being sent, wasting bandwidth. Including the checksum ensures that the packet is dropped and bandwidth is not wasted on a corrupt packet. In modern times, bandwidth is less of a bottleneck, so the checksum is no longer necessary, and it's not a huge performance impact if some corrupt packets are sent all the way through the network.
blocks.zh_html: IPv6 消除了校验和(eliminates checksums)。支持包含校验和(checksum)的论据是：如果分组(packet)被损坏但未被检测到，损坏的分组会继续被发送，浪费带宽(bandwidth)。包含校验和可以确保分组被丢弃，带宽不会浪费在损坏的分组上。在现代，带宽已不再是主要瓶颈，因此校验和不再必要，即使一些损坏的分组被一路发送到网络尽头，也不会造成巨大的性能影响。

blocks.en: IPv6 eliminates fragmentation. If an IPv6 packet is too large for a specific link, the router will drop the packet and send an error message back to the source with the maximum allowable packet size (MTU). The original sender is responsible for splitting up the data into smaller packets and re-sending those smaller packets. End hosts (e.g. your personal computer) process fewer packets than routers (e.g. in data centers), so transferring the workload of fragmentation from routers to end hosts improves the overall scalability of the Internet.
blocks.en_html: IPv6 eliminates fragmentation. If an IPv6 packet is too large for a specific link, the router will drop the packet and send an error message back to the source with the maximum allowable packet size (MTU). The original sender is responsible for splitting up the data into smaller packets and re-sending those smaller packets. End hosts (e.g. your personal computer) process fewer packets than routers (e.g. in data centers), so transferring the workload of fragmentation from routers to end hosts improves the overall scalability of the Internet.
blocks.zh_html: IPv6 消除了分片(eliminates fragmentation)。如果 IPv6 分组(packet)对特定链路(link)来说太大，路由器(router)会丢弃该分组，并向发送方返回一条包含最大允许分组大小(MTU)的错误消息。原始发送方负责将数据拆分成更小的分组并重新发送这些更小的分组。端主机(end hosts)，例如你的个人电脑，处理的分组比路由器少得多，例如数据中心中的路由器，因此将分片的工作量从路由器转移到端主机，提高了互联网(Internet)的整体可扩展性(scalability)。

blocks.en: IPv6 replaces the variable-length options section with a modified implementation of the protocol field. In IPv4, options were problematic because they created variable-length headers, which are harder to parse. In IPv6, the header is fixed in length. This also means that the header length field can be eliminated.
blocks.en_html: IPv6 replaces the variable-length options section with a modified implementation of the protocol field. In IPv4, options were problematic because they created variable-length headers, which are harder to parse. In IPv6, the header is fixed in length. This also means that the header length field can be eliminated.
blocks.zh_html: IPv6 用协议字段(protocol field)的修改版本来替代可变长度(variable-length)选项部分。在 IPv4 中，选项(option)是有问题的，因为它们产生了可变长度的首部，更难解析(parse)。在 IPv6 中，首部(header)是固定长度的。这也意味着首部长度(header length)字段可以被消除。

blocks.en: In order to continue supporting options, IPv6 generalizes the protocol field to allow the IP packet to be passed up for special processing before reaching Layer 4. (Recall, the protocol header in IPv4 is set to either 7 or 19, to indicate which Layer 4 protocol processes the packet next.) The field is renamed from protocol to next header in IPv6.
blocks.en_html: In order to continue supporting options, IPv6 generalizes the protocol field to allow the IP packet to be passed up for special processing before reaching Layer 4. (Recall, the protocol header in IPv4 is set to either 7 or 19, to indicate which Layer 4 protocol processes the packet next.) The field is renamed from protocol to next header in IPv6.
blocks.zh_html: 为了继续支持选项(options)，IPv6 将协议字段(protocol field)通用化，使 IP 分组(IP packet)在到达第 4 层(Layer 4)之前可以被向上传递以进行特殊处理。（回想一下，IPv4 中的协议首部(protocol header)被设置为 6 或 17，以指示接下来由哪个第 4 层协议处理该分组。）在 IPv6 中，该字段从 protocol 重命名为下一个首部(next header)。

blocks.en: If you want an additional protocol to process the IP packet, you can put that protocol’s corresponding number in the next header field. The designers and users of these extra protocols need to agree on which numbers correspond to which protocols, and a standards body organization needs to manage these numbers. Then, the payload can be passed to the additional protocol, which can read an additional header (after the Layer 3 IPv6 header, but before the Layer 4 header) and perform additional processing, before passing the remaining payload to Layer 4.
blocks.en_html: If you want an additional protocol to process the IP packet, you can put that protocol's corresponding number in the next header field. The designers and users of these extra protocols need to agree on which numbers correspond to which protocols, and a standards body organization needs to manage these numbers. Then, the payload can be passed to the additional protocol, which can read an additional header (after the Layer 3 IPv6 header, but before the Layer 4 header) and perform additional processing, before passing the remaining payload to Layer 4.
blocks.zh_html: 如果你希望另一个额外的协议(protocol)来处理 IP 分组(IP packet)，你可以将该协议对应的编号放入下一个首部(next header)字段。这些额外协议的设计者和使用者需要就哪些编号对应哪些协议达成一致，并且需要一个标准制定机构(standards body)来管理这些编号。然后，载荷(payload)可以传递给该额外协议，该协议会读取一个额外的首部(header)（在第 3 层 IPv6 首部之后、第 4 层首部之前），执行额外的处理，再将剩余的载荷传递给第 4 层(Layer 4)。

blocks.en: If the packet has no additional options, then the next header field is the same as the old protocol field, allowing the IP packet to be directly passed up to a Layer 4 protocol with no further processing.
blocks.en_html: If the packet has no additional options, then the next header field is the same as the old protocol field, allowing the IP packet to be directly passed up to a Layer 4 protocol with no further processing.
blocks.zh_html: 如果分组(packet)没有额外的选项(options)，那么下一个首部(next header)字段与原来的协议字段(protocol field)相同，IP 分组(IP packet)可以直接向上传递给第 4 层协议(Layer 4 protocol)，无需进一步处理。

blocks.en: The idea of next headers can be generalized to allow multiple protocols to process the packet after IPv6, but before Layer 4. For example, IPv6 could have a next header for special processing. Then, the special processing protocol’s header can also contain a next header field, which either specifies a Layer 4 protocol, or yet another special processing protocol. This approach is future-proof, because it supports future protocols that haven’t been invented yet. Those future protocols can be added in this next-header approach, without breaking IPv6 or requiring an update to IPv6.
blocks.en_html: The idea of next headers can be generalized to allow multiple protocols to process the packet after IPv6, but before Layer 4. For example, IPv6 could have a next header for special processing. Then, the special processing protocol's header can also contain a next header field, which either specifies a Layer 4 protocol, or yet another special processing protocol. This approach is future-proof, because it supports future protocols that haven't been invented yet. Those future protocols can be added in this next-header approach, without breaking IPv6 or requiring an update to IPv6.
blocks.zh_html: 下一个首部(next header)的思想可以被推广，允许多个协议(protocols)在 IPv6 之后、第 4 层(Layer 4)之前处理分组(packet)。例如，IPv6 可以有一个用于特殊处理的 next header。然后，特殊处理协议的 header 也可以包含一个 next header 字段，它要么指定一个第 4 层协议，要么指定另一个特殊处理协议。这种方法是面向未来的(future-proof)，因为它支持尚未被发明的未来协议。这些未来协议可以通过这种 next header 方式添加，而不会破坏 IPv6 或需要对 IPv6 进行更新。

blocks.en: IPv6 adds a flow label field to the header. At layer 3, packets are sent independently (how one packet is sent doesn’t affect other packets), but in practice, it’s common for many packets to be related in some way. For example, in a video stream between two hosts, there can be many packets being sent between the same two applications. Layer 3 is supposed to treat these packets separately, but in practice, routers have added more advanced systems called middleboxes (e.g. firewalls, intrusion detection systems) that might care about the fact that these packets are part of the same flow, or connection. For example, a firewall might need to read multiple packets from a connection to decide whether that connection should be allowed or blocked. When all packets are sent independently, these middleboxes have to guess whether two packets are related or not (e.g. it notices packets with the same source/destination IP address). IPv6 adds an explicit way to denote that multiple packets are related.
blocks.en_html: IPv6 adds a flow label field to the header. At layer 3, packets are sent independently (how one packet is sent doesn't affect other packets), but in practice, it's common for many packets to be related in some way. For example, in a video stream between two hosts, there can be many packets being sent between the same two applications. Layer 3 is supposed to treat these packets separately, but in practice, routers have added more advanced systems called middleboxes (e.g. firewalls, intrusion detection systems) that might care about the fact that these packets are part of the same flow, or connection. For example, a firewall might need to read multiple packets from a connection to decide whether that connection should be allowed or blocked. When all packets are sent independently, these middleboxes have to guess whether two packets are related or not (e.g. it notices packets with the same source/destination IP address). IPv6 adds an explicit way to denote that multiple packets are related.
blocks.zh_html: IPv6 在首部(header)中添加了一个流标签(flow label)字段。在第 3 层(layer 3)，分组(packets)是独立发送的（一个分组的发送方式不影响其他分组），但在实践中，许多分组通常会以某种方式相互关联。例如，在两端主机(hosts)之间的视频流(video stream)中，同一对应用之间可能会发送大量分组。第 3 层应该分别处理这些分组，但在实践中，路由器(routers)添加了名为中间盒(middleboxes)的更高级系统，例如防火墙(firewalls)、入侵检测系统(intrusion detection systems)，它们可能关心这些分组属于同一个流(flow)或连接(connection)。例如，防火墙可能需要读取一个连接中的多个分组，以决定该连接是否应该被允许或阻止。当所有分组独立发送时，这些中间盒必须猜测两个分组是否相关，例如通过注意到相同源/目的 IP 地址的分组。IPv6 增加了一种显式方式来表示多个分组是相关的。

blocks.en: The version number is unchanged between IPv4 and IPv6. The packet length is unchanged (though renamed from Total Length to Payload Length). TTL is renamed to Hop Limit, though the functionality is unchanged.
blocks.en_html: The version number is unchanged between IPv4 and IPv6. The packet length is unchanged (though renamed from Total Length to Payload Length). TTL is renamed to Hop Limit, though the functionality is unchanged.
blocks.zh_html: 版本号(version number)在 IPv4 和 IPv6 之间保持不变。分组长度(packet length)保持不变（尽管从总长度(Total Length)重命名为有效载荷长度(Payload Length)）。TTL 重命名为跳数限制(Hop Limit)，但功能保持不变。

blocks.en: The Type of Service bits are renamed to Traffic Class, and can still be used to implement some notion of packet priority.
blocks.en_html: The Type of Service bits are renamed to Traffic Class, and can still be used to implement some notion of packet priority.
blocks.zh_html: 服务类型(Type of Service)位被重命名为流量类别(Traffic Class)，仍然可以用于实现某种分组优先级(packet priority)的概念。

blocks.en: In general, IPv6 embraces the end-to-end principle and asks the end host to do the work (fragmentation, verifying checksum and re-sending corrupt packets) when possible. Some fields, like the hop limit or TTL, are fundamentally an IP-level problem, and can’t be implemented by end hosts. (How would the end host help with a packet looping through the network?)
blocks.en_html: In general, IPv6 embraces the end-to-end principle and asks the end host to do the work (fragmentation, verifying checksum and re-sending corrupt packets) when possible. Some fields, like the hop limit or TTL, are fundamentally an IP-level problem, and can't be implemented by end hosts. (How would the end host help with a packet looping through the network?)
blocks.zh_html: 总的来说，IPv6 采纳了端到端原则(end-to-end principle)，并且尽可能要求端主机(end host)来完成工作，例如分片(fragmentation)、验证校验和(checksum)以及重新发送损坏的分组。某些字段，如跳数限制(Hop Limit)或 TTL，本质上是 IP 级别的问题，无法由端主机实现。（端主机如何帮助处理在网络中循环的分组呢？）

blocks.en: IPv6 also tries to simplify the header (removing variable-length options), while still allowing extensibility for future improvements (next-header approach, flow label).
blocks.en_html: IPv6 also tries to simplify the header (removing variable-length options), while still allowing extensibility for future improvements (next-header approach, flow label).
blocks.zh_html: IPv6 还试图简化首部(header)（移除可变长度选项(variable-length options)），同时仍然允许为未来改进提供扩展性(extensibility)，即 next-header 方式和流标签(flow label)。

blocks.en: IP Header Security
blocks.en_html: IP Header Security
blocks.zh_html: IP 首部安全(IP header security)

blocks.en: IP does not have any built-in security against attackers. An attacker could send a packet with an incorrect source IP address, allowing the attacker to impersonate somebody else. This might cause the impersonated host to be wrongly blamed for a packet. Or, if the attacker sends a spoofed packet, the reply may be sent to the impersonated host. Lying about the source address is known as IP spoofing.
blocks.en_html: IP does not have any built-in security against attackers. An attacker could send a packet with an incorrect source IP address, allowing the attacker to impersonate somebody else. This might cause the impersonated host to be wrongly blamed for a packet. Or, if the attacker sends a spoofed packet, the reply may be sent to the impersonated host. Lying about the source address is known as IP spoofing.
blocks.zh_html: IP 没有任何针对攻击者(attackers)的内置安全性。攻击者可以发送带有不正确的源 IP 地址(source IP address)的分组(packet)，从而冒充他人。这可能导致被冒充的主机(host)因该分组而受到错误追究。或者，如果攻击者发送了伪造(spoofed)分组，回复可能会被发送到被冒充的主机。关于源地址的谎报称为IP 欺骗(IP spoofing)。

blocks.en: IP spoofing can be used for denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. A DoS attack can be used to overwhelm a server and cause it to crash by flooding the server with packets. If all the packets came from the same sender, the server could stop the attack by ignoring packets from the attacker’s IP address. However, if the attacker lies about the source IP address, the server has a harder time distinguishing attacker traffic from legitimate traffic.
blocks.en_html: IP spoofing can be used for denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. A DoS attack can be used to overwhelm a server and cause it to crash by flooding the server with packets. If all the packets came from the same sender, the server could stop the attack by ignoring packets from the attacker's IP address. However, if the attacker lies about the source IP address, the server has a harder time distinguishing attacker traffic from legitimate traffic.
blocks.zh_html: IP 欺骗(IP spoofing)可用于拒绝服务(DoS)攻击。DoS 攻击可以通过用大量分组(packets)淹没服务器(server)使其不堪重负并崩溃。如果所有分组来自同一个发送方，服务器可以通过忽略来自攻击者 IP 地址的分组来阻止攻击。然而，如果攻击者谎报源 IP 地址(source IP address)，服务器就更难区分攻击者流量(attacker traffic)和合法流量(legitimate traffic)。

blocks.en: More sophisticated attacks involving spoofing exist, though we won’t cover them in detail in this class (see the UC Berkeley CS 161 notes for more details).
blocks.en_html: More sophisticated attacks involving spoofing exist, though we won't cover them in detail in this class (see the UC Berkeley CS 161 notes for more details).
blocks.zh_html: 还存在更复杂的涉及欺骗(spoofing)的攻击，不过本课程不会详细讨论（更多细节请参阅 UC Berkeley CS 161 的笔记）。

blocks.en: The ToS field in the IP header allows the sender to set a priority on their packets. If we allow everybody to set their own priority, malicious users can set higher priorities and trick the network into prioritizing attacker traffic.
blocks.en_html: The ToS field in the IP header allows the sender to set a priority on their packets. If we allow everybody to set their own priority, malicious users can set higher priorities and trick the network into prioritizing attacker traffic.
blocks.zh_html: IP 首部(IP header)中的 ToS 字段允许发送方为其分组(packets)设置优先级(priority)。如果我们允许每个人设置自己的优先级，恶意用户可以设置更高的优先级，诱使网络优先处理攻击者流量(attacker traffic)。

blocks.en: If the network charges an extra fee for high-priority traffic, the attacker could send a spoofed high-priority packet, and the impersonated host would have to pay for the attacker’s traffic.
blocks.en_html: If the network charges an extra fee for high-priority traffic, the attacker could send a spoofed high-priority packet, and the impersonated host would have to pay for the attacker's traffic.
blocks.zh_html: 如果网络对高优先级流量(high-priority traffic)收取额外费用，攻击者可以发送伪造的(spoofed)高优先级分组(packet)，而被冒充的主机(host)将不得不为攻击者的流量付费。

blocks.en: The original Internet design did not stop these attacks, though modern ISPs (Internet service providers) have implemented additional security measures to mitigate IP layer attacks. In the modern Internet, ISPs don’t allow end hosts to set the ToS field, and many ISPs have tools to detect and block spoofed packets.
blocks.en_html: The original Internet design did not stop these attacks, though modern ISPs (Internet service providers) have implemented additional security measures to mitigate IP layer attacks. In the modern Internet, ISPs don't allow end hosts to set the ToS field, and many ISPs have tools to detect and block spoofed packets.
blocks.zh_html: 最初的互联网(Internet)设计并未阻止这些攻击，不过现代 ISP(Internet service providers，互联网服务提供商)已经实施了额外的安全措施来缓解 IP 层攻击。在现代互联网中，ISP 不允许端主机(end hosts)设置 ToS 字段，并且许多 ISP 拥有检测和阻止伪造(spoofed)分组的工具。

blocks.en: In IPv4, attackers could intentionally send large packets, forcing routers to perform extra work fragmenting those packets. Or, attackers could intentionally add extra options, forcing routers to process those extra options. This could be used to perform DoS attacks and overwhelm a router’s processing capacity.
blocks.en_html: In IPv4, attackers could intentionally send large packets, forcing routers to perform extra work fragmenting those packets. Or, attackers could intentionally add extra options, forcing routers to process those extra options. This could be used to perform DoS attacks and overwhelm a router's processing capacity.
blocks.zh_html: 在 IPv4 中，攻击者可以故意发送大分组(packets)，强制路由器(routers)额外执行分片(fragmenting)操作。或者，攻击者可以故意添加额外的选项(options)，强制路由器处理这些额外选项。这可用于执行 DoS 攻击，压垮路由器的处理能力。

blocks.en: The TTL field can be exploited to learn about the network topology. You could send a packet with TTL 1. The packet will expire at the first hop, and the first router will send you an error message, allowing you to learn the identity of the first router.
blocks.en_html: The TTL field can be exploited to learn about the network topology. You could send a packet with TTL 1. The packet will expire at the first hop, and the first router will send you an error message, allowing you to learn the identity of the first router.
blocks.zh_html: TTL 字段可以被利用来了解网络拓扑(network topology)。你可以发送一个 TTL 为 1 的分组(packet)。该分组会在第一跳(first hop)过期，第一台路由器(router)会向你发送一条错误消息，让你得知第一台路由器的身份。

blocks.en: Then, you can send a packet with TTL 2, which will expire at the second hop. The second router will send you an error message, allowing you to also discover the second router.
blocks.en_html: Then, you can send a packet with TTL 2, which will expire at the second hop. The second router will send you an error message, allowing you to also discover the second router.
blocks.zh_html: 然后，你可以发送一个 TTL 为 2 的分组(packet)，它会在第二跳(second hop)过期。第二台路由器(router)会向你发送一条错误消息，让你也能发现第二台路由器。

blocks.en: By repeating this with TTL 3, TTL 4, and so on, you can discover all the routers on your path. This attack is known as traceroute, though others argue that it’s not an attack and is useful for diagnostics.
blocks.en_html: By repeating this with TTL 3, TTL 4, and so on, you can discover all the routers on your path. This attack is known as traceroute, though others argue that it's not an attack and is useful for diagnostics.
blocks.zh_html: 通过用 TTL 3、TTL 4 等重复这个过程，你可以发现路径上的所有路由器(routers)。这种攻击被称为路由追踪(traceroute)，尽管也有人认为这不是攻击，而是有用的诊断工具。

blocks.en: Repeating this attack on different sources and destinations allows you to learn more of the network topology. Some routers do not send an error message when the TTL is exceeded, which might limit this exploit.
blocks.en_html: Repeating this attack on different sources and destinations allows you to learn more of the network topology. Some routers do not send an error message when the TTL is exceeded, which might limit this exploit.
blocks.zh_html: 对不同的源和目的地重复这种攻击，可以让你了解更多的网络拓扑(network topology)。有些路由器(router)在 TTL 超限时不会发送错误消息，这可能会限制这种利用(exploit)方式。

blocks.en: An attacker could theoretically tamper with the protocol or checksum field, but this would likely cause the packet to be dropped because of an invalid protocol or checksum, so practical attacks with these two fields don’t really exist.
blocks.en_html: An attacker could theoretically tamper with the protocol or checksum field, but this would likely cause the packet to be dropped because of an invalid protocol or checksum, so practical attacks with these two fields don't really exist.
blocks.zh_html: 理论上，攻击者可以篡改协议(protocol)或校验和(checksum)字段，但这很可能会导致分组(packet)因为无效的协议或校验和而被丢弃，因此针对这两个字段的实际攻击并不存在。
